1.1.rationale: In the Indonesian text, Chapter IV regulates “Perlindungan Perempuan” and includes “pencegahan kekerasan terhadap perempuan” (Pasal 30, Pasal 35) and strengthening service institutions for women victims of violence (Pasal 36). However, it never specifies “kekerasan dalam rumah tangga” (domestic violence) or frames violence as occurring in the household/intimate partner context. The judge inferred domestic violence is included simply because ‘violence against women’ is mentioned. That inference is too broad for an indicator specifically about domestic violence scope; the available passages only support general VAW prevention/protection, not DV explicitly.

REGARDING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT
I. GENERAL
The presence of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Regulation as has been amended several times, most recently by Law Number 9 of 2015 concerning the Second Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Regulation and Law Number 33 of 2004 concerning Financial Balance Between the Central Government and Regional Governments constitutes an entry point for Women's Empowerment in regional development. Women's empowerment is an appropriate development strategy to realize gender equality and justice through gender-sensitive and gender-responsive development policies and programs in the future, particularly in North Central Timor Regency.
In North Central Timor Regency there are several conditions that need to be intervened through the establishment of a Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment. This occurs because there is much discrimination against women in developing themselves and opportunities for the fulfillment of their rights. Women are only considered as second-class citizens. Their duty is to take care of the household and they do not need to work. This needs to be fought against, this stigma becomes a problem that must be resolved through empowerment programs.
The above paradigm is reflected in data on the presence of women working in Government, data shows that women are not in strategic positions to participate in making decisions or policies, especially in Government affairs, through data on Civil Servants based on gender available in the field.
Based on this thinking, it is time for North Central Timor Regency to establish a Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment in North Central Timor Regency. This Regional Regulation will regulate the implementation of gender mainstreaming clearly, firmly, in a balanced and comprehensive manner to realize gender equality and justice as well as simultaneously provide understanding about the importance of women's empowerment as a gender analysis strategy in planning, formulating, implementing, monitoring and evaluating development policies and programs.

Article 20
(1) Pokja PUG is responsible for preparing the PUG Implementation Report every 6 (six) months and the five-yearly RAD PUG Implementation Report.
(2) The reporting framework as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be guided by the reporting framework as referred to in the laws and regulations concerning General Guidelines for PUG Implementation in the Regions.
(3) The Pokja PUG report as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be reported to the Regent.
(4) The Regent is responsible for examining and declaring approval of the Pokja PUG Report as referred to in paragraph (1).
(5) The Regent is responsible for sending the pokja PUG report as referred to in paragraph (1) to the Minister who administers Home Affairs governmental matters.

3.5.rationale: The cited Indonesian provisions concern (i) women’s empowerment in the legal field via KIE and “fasilitasi akses dan layanan konsultasi hukum” (Pasal 26(2)(b)), and (ii) strengthening service institutions via “memfasilitasi pelatihan paralegal” (Pasal 36(2)(b)). These are legal awareness/consultation and capacity-building measures, not necessarily legal assistance for survivors (e.g., representation, legal aid for cases, accompaniment in court) as a specialised support service. The judge equated legal consultation and paralegal training with provision of legal assistance services, which is a lenient interpretation not supported explicitly by the text.

Paragraph 1
General

REGARDING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT
I. GENERAL
The presence of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Regulation as has been amended several times, most recently by Law Number 9 of 2015 concerning the Second Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Regulation and Law Number 33 of 2004 concerning Financial Balance Between the Central Government and Regional Governments constitutes an entry point for Women's Empowerment in regional development. Women's empowerment is an appropriate development strategy to realize gender equality and justice through gender-sensitive and gender-responsive development policies and programs in the future, particularly in North Central Timor Regency.
In North Central Timor Regency there are several conditions that need to be intervened through the establishment of a Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment. This occurs because there is much discrimination against women in developing themselves and opportunities for the fulfillment of their rights. Women are only considered as second-class citizens. Their duty is to take care of the household and they do not need to work. This needs to be fought against, this stigma becomes a problem that must be resolved through empowerment programs.
The above paradigm is reflected in data on the presence of women working in Government, data shows that women are not in strategic positions to participate in making decisions or policies, especially in Government affairs, through data on Civil Servants based on gender available in the field.
Based on this thinking, it is time for North Central Timor Regency to establish a Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment in North Central Timor Regency. This Regional Regulation will regulate the implementation of gender mainstreaming clearly, firmly, in a balanced and comprehensive manner to realize gender equality and justice as well as simultaneously provide understanding about the importance of women's empowerment as a gender analysis strategy in planning, formulating, implementing, monitoring and evaluating development policies and programs.

(3) The evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

REGARDING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT
I. GENERAL
The presence of Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Regulation as has been amended several times, most recently by Law Number 9 of 2015 concerning the Second Amendment to Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Regulation and Law Number 33 of 2004 concerning Financial Balance Between the Central Government and Regional Governments constitutes an entry point for Women's Empowerment in regional development. Women's empowerment is an appropriate development strategy to realize gender equality and justice through gender-sensitive and gender-responsive development policies and programs in the future, particularly in North Central Timor Regency.
In North Central Timor Regency there are several conditions that need to be intervened through the establishment of a Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment. This occurs because there is much discrimination against women in developing themselves and opportunities for the fulfillment of their rights. Women are only considered as second-class citizens. Their duty is to take care of the household and they do not need to work. This needs to be fought against, this stigma becomes a problem that must be resolved through empowerment programs.
The above paradigm is reflected in data on the presence of women working in Government, data shows that women are not in strategic positions to participate in making decisions or policies, especially in Government affairs, through data on Civil Servants based on gender available in the field.
Based on this thinking, it is time for North Central Timor Regency to establish a Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment in North Central Timor Regency. This Regional Regulation will regulate the implementation of gender mainstreaming clearly, firmly, in a balanced and comprehensive manner to realize gender equality and justice as well as simultaneously provide understanding about the importance of women's empowerment as a gender analysis strategy in planning, formulating, implementing, monitoring and evaluating development policies and programs.
